title: Natural overlap maps before imposing descent equations
statement: For a category C, a contravariant pseudofunctor F to categories, and a family f_a:X_a→S, natural overlap transitions consist of objects N_a in F(X_a) and morphisms between the pullbacks of N_a and N_b to every Y with compatible maps Y→X_a and Y→X_b over S. These morphisms commute with further pullback, using the pseudofunctor composition comparisons. No identity or composition law is imposed. Coherent means that the transition on equal maps is the identity and transitions compose on every triple of test maps. A comparison to genuine descent data D is a family of object isomorphisms commuting with these transitions. Pullback transitions are constructed by conjugating the transitions on the composite test maps with F's composition comparisons. Coherent transitions give descent data by filling the identity and composition fields. For schemes [def-pc-scheme] and base changes [def-pc-base-change], the refinement map between chart pullbacks is the pullback lift of the later chart projection and base transition. A comparison of the pulled transitions to genuine descent data yields a morphism from the pulled assembled datum, by using its component homs and rewriting the test-map compatibility equation.
